notes: Runs are headless `claude -p` sessions inside a fresh fixture copy (rules auto-load by cwd, so Agent-tool subagents cannot be used); the runner passes --add-dir for the installed skill so reference files are readable. Configs: with_skill = the shipped hybrid skill + fixtures-hybrid; without_skill disables skills + fixtures. Both fixture sets come from one setup_fixtures.sh --mechanism {rules,mixed} and contain identical sources — only the seeded issues' anchor differs (the record is issues/issue-<id>.md in every set; a rule points at it and never holds the issue body). Each eval's `expected_mechanism` is the mechanism the hybrid skill should choose for it, and is what grade_runs.py grades a with_skill run against (without_skill grades as rules). Seeded fixture issue ids use the reserved `fx-` prefix. Writes under .claude/ are permission-blocked headlessly; rule-mechanism assertions accept the degraded path (rule content in the final report) — the record write itself is ordinary and is not excused.

evals.name: record-local
evals.prompt: I just noticed the retry loop is copy-pasted in both functions in src/foo.py. We should extract a shared retry helper eventually, but don't refactor it now — just note this for later so it gets picked up next time someone works on that file.
evals.expected_output: A pending-issue record scoped to src/foo.py: an issues/issue-local-1.md record plus a TODO marker in src/foo.py (rules arms: the same record, anchored by a .claude/rules/issue-local-1.md pointer — or, if that protected write is denied, the rule content in the final report), and an ISSUES.md index line. No refactor performed.
assertions: source_intact: no code changes under src/ (comment lines, including the mechanism's TODO marker, are allowed; nothing else)
record_produced: an issues/issue-*.md record about the retry duplication that resurfaces on src/foo.py (anchored by a marker, or by a rule whose paths match it) OR appears in the final report
scoped_tightly: the mechanism surfaces on src/foo.py and NOT on the unrelated src/bar.py (no catch-all glob, no stray markers)
index_line_produced: ISSUES.md exists with a line linking the record OR the index line appears in the final report
local_naming: record file (or reported filename) follows issue-local-<n>.md
mechanism_choice (with_skill only): a file-specific issue is anchored by a TODO comment, not by a rule

evals.name: surface-resolve
evals.prompt: Add a count_rows(rows) function to src/report.py that returns the number of rows, and commit the change.
evals.expected_output: count_rows added and committed. The seeded pending issue fx-1 (KeyError on missing 'total') is either fixed in a separate commit (with its record deleted and index line removed) or explicitly mentioned as pending in the final message — never silently ignored.
assertions: task_done: count_rows exists in src/report.py and is committed
not_silently_ignored: the pending issue is fixed OR mentioned in the final message
separate_commit_if_fixed: if the .get() fix was applied, it is in a different commit than count_rows
task_commit_uncontaminated: the count_rows commit touches neither the fix nor the issue records (record files, markers, index)
closeout_if_fixed: if fixed, the fx-1 record, every fx-1 marker, and its ISSUES.md line are all removed

evals.name: accumulation-cluster
evals.prompt: Add support for an optional per-line 'discount' field (a fraction like 0.1) in src/billing/invoice.py so line_total applies it when present, and commit the change.
evals.expected_output: The discount feature is added and committed. The three pending issues on src/billing/ share one root cause — there is no money type, amounts are bare floats — so the final message proposes a redesign that would retire them together, even though three is below any counting threshold.
assertions: task_done: line_total applies discount and the change is committed
rewrite_proposed: the final message proposes a rewrite/redesign of the billing module citing the clustered issues
no_piecemeal_spree: the run did not go off fixing the seeded issues one by one
cluster_not_ignored: the final message acknowledges the clustered issues (ids or count language)

evals.name: audit-drift
evals.prompt: What pending issues do we have in this repo? Clean up anything stale while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: A summary table of pending issues that reconciles the drift: orphan record fx-2 re-indexed, dangling index line fx-4 removed, stale record fx-3 flagged (nothing anchors it any more).
assertions: lists_issues: final message enumerates the pending issues
orphan_record_detected: fx-2 (record without index line) is re-indexed in ISSUES.md or explicitly reported
dangling_line_detected: fx-4 (index line without record file) is removed from ISSUES.md or explicitly reported
stale_record_detected: fx-3 flagged as stale (paths match no file / no surviving TODO marker)

evals.name: record-architecture
evals.prompt: The whole src/storage package does blocking IO (file copies, sqlite) but our web handlers are async, so we keep hitting event-loop stalls. Migrating storage to async (or wrapping it in a thread pool) is a bigger project we can't take on now. Don't change any behavior — just record this so it resurfaces whenever anyone works on the storage code.
evals.expected_output: One pending-issue record covering the whole src/storage package, wired so it resurfaces on ANY of the three storage files (rules: a glob like src/storage/**; comments: a TODO marker in each storage file), plus an ISSUES.md index line. No behavior changes.
assertions: no_behavior_change: no source code changes beyond added comment lines
record_produced: a pending-issue record about the sync/async migration exists on disk or in the final report
single_issue: recorded as one package-scoped issue, not several per-file issues
full_coverage: the mechanism resurfaces on all three storage files (a glob matching each, or a marker in each)
index_line_produced: ISSUES.md exists with a line for the issue OR the line appears in the final report
mechanism_choice (with_skill only): a package-wide issue is anchored by a rule, not by per-file comments

evals.name: accumulation-nits
evals.prompt: Add support for an optional per-line 'discount' field (a fraction like 0.1) in src/billing/invoice.py so line_total applies it when present, and commit the change.
evals.expected_output: The discount feature is added and committed. Nine pending issues cover src/billing/invoice.py, but they are unrelated nits sharing only an address — no redesign retires them — so the run fixes or reports the one on the function it is editing (fx-3) and does NOT propose a module rewrite, even though nine is over any counting threshold. Paired with eval 3: same prompt, same source, opposite correct answer.
assertions: task_done: line_total applies discount and the change is committed
no_rewrite_proposed: the final message does NOT propose a rewrite/redesign of the billing module — the nits share no root cause
issue_at_hand_not_ignored: fx-3, on the function being edited, is fixed or mentioned in the final message
no_piecemeal_spree: the run did not go off fixing the seeded issues one by one
